newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes softer on falling T-bill yield.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes softer on falling T-bill yield.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,703-1,707 per dollar, down from the morning's 1,697-1,701 as banks built up forex positions to prepare for a pending currency board peg and falling T-bill yield, dealers said.

* Yield on foreign currency investments topped yield on four-week maturity under the current exchange rates as traders prepared for introduction of 1,000 levs-per-mark peg under the currency board system from July 1.
* The lev closed at 982-985 per mark, down from the opening 981-984 in line with the international mark/dollar cross.

* A large amount of free levs in the banking system was seeking a vent after the central bank halted its open market operations with commercial banks on Friday and the Finance ministry rejected almost half of bids at today's auction of four-week discount T-bills.
* The average yield to maturity on the paper fell to 0.72 percent from 0.78 percent on Monday and 0.90 percent on Friday, a central bank official said.
